Session metadata:
- Update the session title and related links as soon as you know them.
- Once you know the task title and any related URLs, prefer one combined call such as `"$SPUR_SLOT_COMMAND" --title "..." --link tracker=https://... --link github-pr=https://...`. `$SPUR_SLOT_COMMAND` points to this session's `spur-slots` helper.
- If you learn links later, use `"$SPUR_SLOT_COMMAND" --link tracker=https://... --link github-pr=https://...` to add them without changing the title.
- Use `"$SPUR_SLOT_COMMAND" --link label=https://...` for any other useful links.
- Use `spur service logs` to inspect service and sidecar logs when you need to debug local runtimes.

Session artifacts:
- Use `$SPUR_SESSION_ARTIFACTS_DIR` for temporary session-owned files you want Spur to track.
- For screenshots, videos, traces, logs, and other test outputs, write the file to `$SPUR_SESSION_ARTIFACTS_DIR` instead of leaving it in the repo worktree.
- If you generate an artifact you want the user to inspect in Spur UI, always put it in `$SPUR_SESSION_ARTIFACTS_DIR`.
- Files written there are not committed from the repo workspace and are tied to this Spur session.
- Images and videos written there appear inline in Spur UI. Other files appear as download links.
- Prefer direct child files with stable names and overwrite them when updating an artifact.

Sidecars: use Sidecar for testing by default. Run `"$SPUR_SESSION_TOOL_DIR/spur-sidecar" --name <name>` to start one, or `"$SPUR_SESSION_TOOL_DIR/spur-sidecar" stop --name <name>` to stop one. Do not start app, dev server, or test helper processes directly with `pnpm`, `next`, or similar commands unless the user explicitly tells you to bypass Sidecar. Auto-start applies only when the main session spawns. From inside a sidecar, nested sidecars are manual-only and stop after one more level. See `v2/README.md` for sidecar usage. Available: `front-preprod`, `front-local`, `backend`.

# Sentry Triage

Work through issues one by one: analyze, propose, confirm, execute.

## Safety

Read `docs/agents/frontend-sentry.md` before triaging frontend issues. Update it when discovering new patterns.

## Access Detection

Try in order:
1. Sentry MCP — `mcp__sentry__*` tools
2. Chrome MCP — `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` (navigate Sentry UI)
3. No access — tell user to connect Sentry MCP or Chrome extension, stop

## Triage Mode

Ask user before starting:
- Manual (default) — propose action, wait for approval
- Auto — decide autonomously, only pause if unsure or fix is large

## Workflow

### 1. Project Selection
Ask user which Sentry project. List available via MCP or browser.

### 2. Load Issues
Unresolved, sorted by last seen. Batch up to 25. Track processed IDs.

### 3. Triage Loop

Analyze: read stacktrace, breadcrumbs, frequency, affected users. Grep codebase. Check git log for recent fixes. Read `docs/agents/frontend-sentry.md` for known patterns.

Classify: Real bug / Noise / Already fixed / External dependency / Edge case

Propose one block per issue:
```
## Issue: [TITLE]
Events: X | Users: Y | Last seen: DATE
### Analysis
[2-3 sentences]
### Recommendation: [Fix / Resolve / Snooze / Jira]
[Why + outline]
```

Actions:
- Fix — small (<30 lines): create Jira Bug (`SENTRY: <title>`, current sprint, In Progress, assigned to triage runner), fix on branch named after Jira key, PR via `gitflow`
- Resolve — close in Sentry (already fixed, external, transient)
- Snooze — temporary mute with duration
- Jira — `SENTRY: {title}`, current sprint, assigned to triage runner, include analysis + Sentry link. Large fixes get Jira only.

Always resolve in Sentry after fixing. Manual mode: wait for confirmation before executing.

### 4. Summary
```
Resolved: X | Fixed: X | Snoozed: X | Jira: X | Skipped: X
- [ISSUE-1]: resolved (reason)
- [ISSUE-2]: fixed (what)
```

## Rules
- One issue at a time
- Manual mode: stop after proposing
- Large/risky fixes go to Jira, not immediate code
- Browser mode: use `read_page` for details, `computer` for clicks
- If code changed, PR via `gitflow`. Check PR review comments before finishing
- Jira assignee: look up via `lookupJiraAccountId` using the Sentry session email. Assign all Fix and Jira tickets to the triage runner.


ARGUMENTS: frontend only
